reason: The text demonstrates that Yahweh ('יהוה') is actively present with and devoted to the wellbeing of Joseph, who is explicitly identified as a Hebrew person ('אִ֥ישׁ עִבְרִ֖י'). The repeated affirmation 'וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֔ף' (And the LORD was with Joseph) is coupled with consistent blessing and prosperity ('אִ֣ישׁ מַצְלִ֑יחַ'—a successful/prosperous man). Notably, Yahweh's protective care continues even when Joseph faces severe injustice and imprisonment, ensuring his success and well-being under adversity. This pattern of divine solicitude toward a Hebrew individual's welfare—prosperity in servitude, favor with authority figures, and preservation through false accusation—exemplifies Yahweh's active commitment to the flourishing of at least the Hebrew people represented in this text.
